newsitem.title: ITALY: Committal hearing for Italian PM may be postponed.
newsitem.headline: Committal hearing for Italian PM may be postponed.

text.p: A committal hearing to decide whether Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi should stand trial over alleged irregularities during his chairmanship of state holding IRI, might be postponed, judicial sources said on Monday.

The hearing is set for January 15, but could be immediately adjourned because a lawyer representing another former IRI board member who faces similar charges to Prodi, is busy with another case in Turin.
An Italian magistrate recommended in November that Prodi and five other members of the IRI board should be tried for alleged abuse of office and conflict of interest.

The request relates to the sale by IRI in October 1993 of the food company Cirio, best known for its canned tomatoes, to a southern Italian consortium, Fis.Vi. The magistrate alleges IRI's board granted the buyer an "unjust advantage" in the sale.
Prodi, who has led a centre-left government since last May and was chairman of IRI for most of the 1980s and again in 1993, has denied the accusations.
